## Module Exports (`dealbreaker`)

### `init(moduleOrPath?: InitInput): Promise<void>`

Initialize the WebAssembly module. Safe to call multiple times.

In Node.js, the module is initialized automatically on import, so calling `init()` is optional.
In browsers and bundlers, `await init()` must resolve before calling `presets()` or constructing
a `Solver`.

### `presets(): PresetInfo[]`

List all built-in game presets.

### `formatStep(step: Step | string): string`

Format a single step as human-readable text (e.g. `"tableau 4 -> cell 1"`).

## `class Solver`

One game's compiled rules. Create once, reuse across many positions.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `constructor(rules: Rules \| string)` | Compile a game from a `Rules` object or rules JSON string. |
| `static fromPreset(id: string): Solver` | Compile a built-in preset by id (see `presets()`). |
| `rules(): Rules` | The game's compiled rules. |
| `deal(seed: number): StateData` | Deal a position from a seed (0 to 2^53). |
| `dealMicrosoft(n: number): StateData` | Deal Microsoft FreeCell deal `n` (1 to 2^31 - 1). |
| `dealOrdered(cards: readonly string[] \| string): StateData` | Deal an explicit card order (`cards[0]` dealt first), e.g. `["AS", "2S", ...]`. |
| `validate(state: StateData \| string): void` | Validate a position against this game's pack and pile capacities. Throws if invalid. |
| `solve(state: StateData \| string, options?: SolveOptions \| string): SolveResult` | Solve a position. |
| `best(state: StateData \| string, options?: SolveOptions \| string): MaxResult` | For games played for points: find the line of play that ends with the most points. |
| `score(state: StateData \| string): number \| null` | Points for a position, or `null` for games not played for points. |
| `hint(state: StateData \| string, options?: HintOptions \| string): Hint \| null` | Suggest a next step without peeking at face-down cards, or `null` if no win was found. |
| `grade(state: StateData \| string, options?: GradeOptions \| string): Difficulty` | Grade a deal as easy, medium or hard. Thresholds are calibrated per preset for the default budgets; unwinnable deals, and deals not won within the budget, are hard. |
| `legalSteps(state: StateData \| string): Step[]` | Every legal single step in this position. |
| `playStep(state: StateData \| string, step: Step \| string): StateData` | Play one step and return the resulting position. Throws if the step is illegal. |
| `isWon(state: StateData \| string): boolean` | Whether the position is won. |
| `render(state: StateData \| string): string` | Render a position as a human-readable ASCII board. |
| `free(): void` | Free the underlying WebAssembly instance. |

## `class WorkerSolver` (`dealbreaker/worker`)

Runs a Dealbreaker `Solver` inside a dedicated Web Worker so searches never block the UI thread.
Call `terminate()` to stop the worker and cancel any in-flight search.

|---|---|
| `static fromPreset(id: string, wasmUrl?: URL \| string): Promise<WorkerSolver>` |  |

| `dealMicrosoft(n: number): Promise<StateData>` |  |

## Core Data & Result Types

For the full `Rules` type tree, see the [Rules Schema Reference](/reference/rules-schema).

```ts
/**
 * A position keyed by group name. Cards are bottom-first, e.g. `"AS"`, `"10H"`, `"~KC"` (face down),
 * or `"JK"` / `"~JK"` (joker). In `hint()`, unknown face-down cards may be written as `"?"` or `"~?"`.
 */
export interface StateData {
  piles: Record<string, string[][]>;
  redeals_used?: number;
  base_rank?: number;
  seed?: number;
}

export interface PileRef {
  group: string;
  index: number;
}

export type Step =
  | { type: "deal" }
  | { type: "redeal" }
  | { type: "move"; from: PileRef; to: PileRef; count: number }
  | { type: "remove"; piles: PileRef[] };

export type Strategy = "auto" | "depth_first" | "best_first";

export interface SolveOptions {
  strategy?: Strategy;
  max_states?: number;
  /** Wall-clock timeout in milliseconds (enforced on native targets). */
  timeout_ms?: number;
  autoplay?: boolean;
  shorten?: boolean;
}

export type OutcomeLabel = "solved" | "unsolvable" | "gave-up";

export interface SolveResult {
  outcome: OutcomeLabel;
  states: number;
  steps?: Step[];
}

export interface MaxResult {
  score: number;
  proven: boolean;
  states: number;
  steps: Step[];
}

export interface HintOptions {
  samples?: number;
  solve?: SolveOptions;
  seed?: number;
}

export interface Hint {
  step: Step;
  wins: number;
  samples: number;
  score?: number;
}

export interface GradeThresholds {
  /** Winnable deals scoring below this are easy. */
  medium: number;
  /** Winnable deals scoring below this (and at least `medium`) are medium; the rest are hard. */
  hard: number;
}

export interface GradeOptions {
  /** Main search budget in distinct positions (default 500000). */
  max_states?: number;
  /** Positions along the winning line at which every move is tried (default 10). */
  probe_positions?: number;
  /** Budget for each move tried (default 3000). */
  probe_states?: number;
  /** Cut-offs to use instead of the game's built-in ones. */
  thresholds?: GradeThresholds;
}

export type Grade = "easy" | "medium" | "hard";

export interface Difficulty {
  grade: Grade;
  /** `true`: won; `false`: proven unwinnable; `null`: budget ran out. Only `true` can be easy or medium. */
  winnable: boolean | null;
  /** `log2(1 + effort) + 10 * trap_rate`, for winnable deals. */
  score?: number;
  /** Distinct positions the main search visited. */
  effort: number;
  /** Moves tried along the winning line. */
  probes: number;
  /** Moves tried that the solver couldn't win from within the probe budget. */
  traps: number;
  trap_rate: number;
  /** Length of the winning line found, in single steps (0 if none). */
  steps: number;
  thresholds: GradeThresholds;
  /** `preset`: calibrated for this game; `custom`: from options; `generic`: no calibration for this game. */
  source: "preset" | "custom" | "generic";
}

export interface PresetInfo {
  id: string;
  name: string;
}

export type InitInput =
  | RequestInfo
  | URL
  | Response
  | BufferSource
  | WebAssembly.Module;
```
